title: The Four-Hundred-Dollar Compliment
logline: Lily, undefeated for nine years at getting people to do things, is outmaneuvered in a grocery line by Quinn, who wasn't even trying, and launches a covert war of manipulations fought entirely through an oblivious Barney. Ted appoints himself commissioner, Robin and Marshall bet on the outcome, and Barney has the greatest week of his life, because every idea he has is somehow brilliant.
coldOpen: Kids, for nine years your Aunt Lily was the undefeated champion of getting people to do things. Then one Monday, in a grocery line, she lost her title to a woman who wasn't even trying.

couch.line: Is this the time Aunt Lily cried in a grocery store?
She says it was the onions. She was in the chip aisle.

guests.name: Augie Pappalardo
guests.role: Owner of Augie's Market on Ninth Avenue and a former Golden Gloves ring announcer. Announces every grocery total like a title fight, and in nine years of ringing up Lily has never once seen her wallet

scenes.summary: Lily closes a three-week con to make Barney pay for the rooftop party groceries. Quinn walks in, credits Barney with Lily's 'generous offer', invents a dance company and a dog, and Lily pays and thanks her. Quinn gives Barney the credit. Lily declares a covert war, Robin bets on Quinn, Marshall on Lily, and Ted appoints himself commissioner.

beats.line: It started five days before the first rooftop party of summer, at Augie's Market on Ninth Avenue.
Barney, it's sweet you're buying the regular steaks. Very humble. Very middle management.
Regular? Lily, these are prime.
Prime's fine. The Wagyu's back there, but that's for men who've really made it.
Lily, I've made it. I have a guy who irons my money.
Nine years together, I've never seen my wife's wallet. I'm not sure she owns one.
Nine years she shops here. Never paid once. I figured she was royalty.
Augie. The Wagyu, the whole cart and whatever the lady's having. Put it on the Stinson.
Hey, babe. Hi, everybody. Oh my god, Lily.
Quinn.
Barney told me you insisted on getting the groceries this year. That is so generous.
I said that?
Last night. You got a little choked up.
I told my whole dance company. Twelve dancers. Two cried. One's naming her dog Lily.
What kind of dog?
A rescue. She's got a limp. She never gives up.
Augie, what's the total?
Four hundred twelve dollars, and sixty cents!
Is that a wallet? She has a wallet!
Thank you.
For what?
I genuinely don't know.
Babe, that was so smart.
I know. What did I do?
All you.
Lily. Did you just get played in a grocery line by a compliment?
It was a really good compliment, Robin. There's a dog.
Baby, you paid. At our wedding, you got the caterer to tip us.
She didn't even break stride. She did it on her way to the hummus.
Lily, you can't play Barney against his own girlfriend.
Somebody has to play him, Ted. Have you seen him unsupervised?
Twenty bucks on Quinn.
Nine years of you meddling in my love life, Lily. I want this so bad I can taste the hummus.
Forty on my wife. That's not romance, Ted. I've seen her work. It's terrifying.
Then this needs a commissioner. Someone impartial, with rules, a chart and beautiful handwriting.
Nobody said you, Ted.
Nobody had to.
Four hundred and twelve dollars. That's an expensive lesson.
And sixty cents.
Kids, your Aunt Lily kept that receipt. She tells people it's for her taxes. Your Aunt Lily has never once done her own taxes.

scenes.summary: Barney's heroic version of the grocery store. Ted unveils the official standings, disguised from Barney as fantasy curling. Lily's round two: she goads Barney into wearing sweatpants to the roof. Quinn lets herself in with her key and flips it: Lily is the one wearing sweatpants Saturday, Barney keeps his suit, and the commissioner is bought with one compliment about his lettering. Lily thanks her again.

beats.line: Two days later, Barney had worked up his own version of events.
And that is how I got Lily Aldrin to buy four hundred dollars of meat.
I looked you dead in the eye and snapped you like a breadstick.
Lily. You're paying.
Please, Barney, have mercy! I'm just a simple kindergarten teacher with no cunning at all!
Babe. You're a genius. And so much taller than I remembered.
The winner, and still champion of Ninth Avenue!
And Quinn has never once called you tall.
Agree to disagree. My version has a ring announcer.
Round one to Quinn. Commissioner's note: unforced error, devastating compliment.
beats.title: Official Standings, Commissioner T. Mosby

beats.line: Round two. By Saturday, Barney will be on that roof in sweatpants. And he'll think it was his idea.
Lily, he's never worn sweatpants. He wore a suit to his own colonoscopy.
That's not a scheme. That's an exorcism.
What's on the chart?
Fantasy curling.
Nerds.
Barney, did you know the most confident men in Manhattan are switching to sweatpants? Suits are for men who need help.
Sweatpants are a white flag for your legs.
You're right. You couldn't pull them off. You need the suit. It's like a security blanket. With lapels.
Couldn't pull them off? Lily, I could pull off a cape at a funeral.
Saturday. The roof. Sweatpants.
Challenge acc—
Hey, babe. Used my key.
Babe! I'm wearing sweatpants to the roof on Saturday. My idea.
Love that. So brave. And you'll match Lily. She's wearing sweatpants Saturday too, she told me.
Match? Like a couple at a theme park? Barney Stinson does not match. Lily, keep the sweatpants. I'm wearing the suit.
I am not wearing sweatpants!
Lily, you told me. Right in front of Marshall.
Did she?
You were eating, Marshall.
Then I can't rule it out.
Ted, is that your lettering on the curling chart? It's gorgeous.
It's architectural block. Thank you for noticing. Two points, Quinn.
Thank you.
Why do I keep saying that?
You're welcome.
Ted, put me down for a point on your little curling chart.
Barney, you're not on the chart.
Then it's a very inaccurate chart.

scenes.summary: Barney's first subway ride, which was his idea after Quinn said it. Ted and Robin call the duel in whispers like sportscasters. Lily corners Quinn on the train; Quinn wins Marshall over with a Brooklyn pie and reveals she isn't playing Lily at all. Barney raves about his heater week of good ideas. Lily misreads it as Quinn building him up to own him, and plans to expose her on the roof tomorrow.

beats.line: That Friday, something happened that had never happened in the history of New York. Barney Stinson rode the subway.
So this is the subway. It's like a limo that hates you.
Quinn said limos are bad for the planet. So I said, then Barney Stinson takes the subway. My idea.
I'm an environmental lawyer! I've been saying that for nine years!
Well, it never sounded like an idea when you said it.
Welcome back to the Lily-Quinn invitational. Lily has changed seats three times to get next to Quinn.
Thanks, Ted. You can feel the tension on the downtown six. Somebody's eating an egg.
Quinn! What a coincidence, you on this train.
You got on at four different stops, Lily. You live the other direction.
That jacket is incredible. Where's it from?
A store where you pay for things, Lily. You'd hate it.
Marshall, I brought you something. Pie, from the Brooklyn place you won't stop talking about.
Lilypad. It's the Brooklyn pie. Sour cherry. I'm switching sides.
You bet forty dollars on me!
And I'll lose it with dignity and a full stomach.
Fine. Let's be honest. You've been beating me all week.
Lily, I'm not playing you.
Everyone knows we're playing. There's a chart. It has lettering.
Architectural block.
I know about the chart. I'm just not playing you.
Then who are you playing?
Nice try, Lily.
Dad, is this a love story or a heist?
Yes.
This is the greatest week of my life. Do you know how many times you people have said, terrible idea, Barney?
We don't keep count.
Four thousand one hundred and six.
And this week? Zero. I'm on a heater. I'm basically a genius now.
You really are, babe. This is our stop.
I knew that. Pure instinct. Ted, mark it down. Subway, conquered.
I see it now. She's building him a throne out of fake good ideas. And once he's sitting on it, she owns him.
Lily, that's just called a relationship.
Tomorrow, on the roof, I show him every idea he had this week was hers. He'll rebel. She's finished.
Lily, that would crush him.
Ted, it's Barney. He's ninety percent confidence and ten percent hair gel. He'll bounce.
Lilypad, that's a dark plan.
Marshall, tomorrow I'm wearing sweatpants in public. I have nothing left to lose.

scenes.summary: The first rooftop of summer. Lily, in sweatpants, exposes Quinn's week to Barney and watches his face fall. She realizes what Quinn was doing and reverses: she claims she was trying to rattle him all week and he beat her three times. Ted rules Barney the winner and the house keeps the pot. At the ledge Quinn explains: Barney thinks they keep him around because he pays, so for one week he didn't, and every idea was good. Lily confesses she does the same for Marshall. Quinn thanks her. Marshall overhears and Lily covers instantly. The gang now protects Barney's terrible plaque idea.

beats.line: Saturday. The first rooftop of summer. Your Aunt Lily came dressed for war.
Lily, those look really comfortable.
I know. I've never been this relaxed and this angry at the same time.
Commissioner's note: Quinn awarded one bonus point for asking about my serifs.
beats.title: Final Round Standings

beats.line: Daddy's home! And yes, the suit was my idea.
Barney. Quick question, for the man having the greatest week of his life.
Fire away, sweatpants.
The grocery store. Whose idea was it that I pay?
Mine.
Was it? Or did Quinn say it first?
Quinn said it first.
And the suit? The subway?
Quinn. And Quinn.
Huh. So none of it was me.
For a second there, I thought I was the smart one.
Which is exactly what I wanted you to think.
I've spent all week trying to get in your head, Barney. Make you doubt yourself. It didn't work. You beat me. Three times.
I beat Lily Aldrin?
The commissioner has reviewed the week. Barney Stinson, three. Lily, zero.
Lily Aldrin, beaten by Barney Stinson! Ted! I need a plaque!
Wait. Who wins my twenty bucks?
Nobody bet on Barney. The house wins.
You're the house.
It's for the plaque.
You had me. Why'd you fold?
Because I finally figured out who you were playing for.
Every check. Every round. Every limo. He thinks that's why you guys keep him around.
That's not why.
I know. So for one week he didn't pay for anything, and every idea he had was a good one.
Because they were yours.
He doesn't need to know whose they were.
And the subway?
Oh, that one was just funny.
I do the same thing for Marshall. He thinks proposing on this roof was his idea.
I know. You tell that story like a bank job.
You're very good, Quinn.
You just lost on purpose so my boyfriend could feel like a genius. You're better.
Thank you, Lily.
Oh, wow. That is so much better from this side.
Wait. Proposing on the roof wasn't my idea?
Of course it was your idea, Marshmallow.
I knew it!
Plaque idea! Bronze. Twelve feet. Bolted to the water tower. Barney Stinson, undefeated.
Barney, that is a terrible—
Ted.
Terribly brilliant idea. Twelve feet? Make it fourteen.
Kids, Barney still brags he beat Lily Aldrin. She's backed him at two weddings and a deposition. It's the only secret she's ever kept.
